exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Ether (ETH) traded at $2,380.91 as of 2026-11-04 15:01:58 UTC, +2.33% over one hour and +4.23% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $2,226.51 to $2,335.68; spot sits at 141% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is +1.67% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($2,295.81) is above the 72-hour average ($2,277.57). Spot is 0.00% below the seven-day high of $2,380.91 and 8.64% above the seven-day low of $2,191.63.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.65% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 78.6, conventionally overbought.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $12.12 billion, equal to 4.17% of the $290.81 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 34 ("Fear"), versus 51 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink ETH/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $2,340.15, 19 minutes before the spot quote and -1.71% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price has surged 4.23% in the past twenty‑four hours and sits 141% above the 24‑hour range midpoint, evidencing a clear upward breakout that, per Exhibit A and B, should propel prices toward the recent seven‑day high of $2,380.91.  

2. Momentum is strong: the 14‑hour RSI is 78.6 (Exhibit D) and the 24‑hour average ($2,295.81) already exceeds the 72‑hour average ($2,277.57) (Exhibit C), indicating bullish pressure that typically precedes further gains.  

3. Liquidity remains robust with $12.12 billion traded in 24 hours (Exhibit E), and although sentiment turned fearful at a Fear & Greed Index of 34 (Exhibit F), such contrarian fear often precedes a rally; the Chainlink feed at $2,340.15 (Exhibit G) provides a solid, lower‑bias entry point for a long practice position.  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is firmly above the 24‑hour range midpoint, sitting at 141 % of that range, indicating a sustained upward thrust rather than a fleeting spike; this price pressure is corroborated by the seven‑day average remaining above the 72‑hour average, a classic bullish continuation signal (Ex. B, C).  

2. Liquidity is robust, with $12.12 billion traded in the last day—4.17 % of market cap—ensuring that any short‑term corrective pullback would be absorbed without triggering a sharp reversal, thereby protecting a short position from premature squeeze (Ex. E).  

3. Although the Fear & Greed Index has dipped to 34, the price has still risen 2.33 % in the past hour and 4.23 % in 24 hours, showing that fear is already priced in and the market is primed for a technical retracement toward the seven‑day low at $2,191.63 (Ex. F, A, C).  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point collapses under Exhibit D: a 78.6 RSI signals extreme overbought conditions, implying an imminent pull‑back that outweighs any “midpoint” argument from Exhibit B. The second point misstates liquidity; while Exhibit E shows $12.12 billion traded, that is only 4.17 % of market cap, insufficient to absorb a rapid unwind when sentiment is fearful (Exhibit F). Thus the market cannot sustain the price and a short correction is far more probable. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s breakout claim collapses on Exhibit B: the 24‑hour range tops at $2,335.68, yet the spot sits at $2,380.91—well beyond the range, indicating a statistical outlier rather than a sustainable trend. Such a gap often precedes rapid correction, not continuation.  

Second, the Bull’s reliance on RSI ignores Exhibit D’s volatility figure: 2.65% daily realized volatility signals a jittery market where an overbought RSI (78.6) is a classic precursor to a pull‑back, not a bullish catalyst.  

Thus, the evidence forecloses any reasonable expectation of further upside. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds a short practice position justified.

findings.finding: Spot price rose 4.23% in 24h, indicating recent buying pressure
RSI 78.6 shows overbought conditions, a known precursor to pull‑back
Fear & Greed Index at 34 signals market fear, often preceding downside moves
Chainlink feed trails spot by 1.71%, offering a lower entry for shorts

ruling.opinion: The price surge (Ex. A) is tempered by extreme overbought momentum (Ex. D) and heightened fear (Ex. F). Overbought RSI combined with modest realized volatility (2.65%/day) suggests the rally is unsustainable. The Chainlink feed lag (Ex. G) provides a lower reference point, reinforcing the case for a short position. While liquidity is ample (Ex. E), it does not offset the bearish technical signals, leading the Court to endorse a short practice trade.
ruling.dissent: Bull counsel emphasizes breakout momentum and volume, but overbought RSI and fear index outweigh those factors, making a short stance more compelling.
